2001.summary: From Mar 2000–Feb 2001, the fund delivered a net 6.3% total return, substantially outperforming the S&P 500’s –9.87%. Growth & Income returned –8.4%, Small Cap +9.1%, and Value +18.3% as AUM rose to $1.9137M, and the fund paid a 5% distribution (~$95,700) to the University of Oklahoma.

2002.summary: In Sep 2001–Aug 2002, the fund generated –9.94% versus a –11.42% blended benchmark, outperforming by 1.48% with alpha of +0.16% monthly. The Fixed Income sleeve launched on May 20, 2002, and the fund paid its 5% dividend to the University of Oklahoma.

2003.summary: In Sep 2002–Aug 2003, the fund returned +6.19% net of fees versus +10.82% for its blended benchmark (underperforming by 4.63%), as net assets grew to $1.716M following three 5% distributions. Volatility tracked benchmarks closely with reduced drawdowns.

2004.summary: From Sep 2003–Aug 2004, amid a strong late‑2003 equity rebound, the Small‑Cap sleeve gained +14.9% versus +11.4% for the Russell 2000, and the fund posted positive net returns while maintaining a healthy cash buffer and paying its 5% dividend to the University of Oklahoma.

2005.summary: In Sep 2004–Aug 2005, the fund achieved +12.7% versus a +14.1% blended benchmark (underperforming by 1.4 pp); Fixed Income returned +2.0% versus Vanguard’s +4.0%, Growth & Value matched benchmarks, and Small Cap outperformed at +28.3%. A 5% dividend was distributed to the University of Oklahoma.

2006.summary: From Sep 2005–Aug 2006, the fund produced +4.12% net of fees versus a 5‑year CAGR of +4.45% (underperforming by 33 bp), supported by positive net inflows across all sleeves, and paid its 5% distribution to the University of Oklahoma.

2007.summary: During early subprime turmoil, the fund produced a net 9.55% total return versus an 11.92% blended benchmark, with Growth at 12.31%, Small Cap at 6.27%, and Value at 15.04% as AUM increased to $1.95M. Enhanced risk controls were implemented, and the fund paid a 5% distribution to the University of Oklahoma.

2008.summary: In Sep 2007–Aug 2008, the Fixed Income sleeve returned +5.34% (Vanguard +5.79%), while equity sleeves underperformed amid market sell‑offs. Risk controls were bolstered with expanded VaR and stress‑testing, and the fund paid its 5% dividend to the University of Oklahoma.

2009.summary: In Sep 2008–Aug 2009, the Fixed Income sleeve rebounded +8.65% versus +7.90% for Vanguard, as equity sleeves recovered from crisis lows. The fund re‑entered credit markets in Q1 ’09 and completed its annual 5% payout to the University of Oklahoma.

2010.summary: From Sep 2009–Aug 2010, investment income rose to $34.6K (from $30.5K), and a 5% distribution of $80.2K was paid. In May 2010, $138.6K was reallocated from Fixed Income and $37.9K from Value into Growth and Small Cap to capture post‑crisis opportunities.

2011.summary: From Sep 2010–Aug 2011, the fund delivered a 12.5% net total return, outperforming its blended benchmark return of 9.5%. In March 2011, the ESG sub-fund was launched to integrate sustainability criteria into stock selection. Net assets increased to $1.75M, and the fund paid a 5% dividend (~$87,500) to the University of Oklahoma.

2012.summary: From Sep 2011–Aug 2012, the fund returned 9.13% over twelve months, trailing its benchmark’s 13.56% and falling 0.94% in the second half. Heightened market drawdowns in May led to a 6.6% cash position by year-end. Net assets stood at $1.60M, and a 5% distribution of $80,000 was paid to Oklahoma.

2013.summary: From Sep 2012–Aug 2013, the fund achieved an 11.71% total return, underperforming its blended benchmark by 4.06%. The Value sleeve outperformed its index by 6.51%, while Growth and Small Cap lagged, and Fixed Income matched its benchmark. The fund paid a 5% dividend ($90,000) and increased AUM to $1.80M.

2014.summary: From Sep 2013–Aug 2014, the fund returned 18.55%, slightly ahead of its blended benchmark’s 18.38%, led by a 14.9% gain in Small Cap and strong fixed-income performance. ESG ratings were increasingly used to guide sector allocation. Net assets rose to $2.10M, and a 5% dividend ($105,000) was paid to the University of Oklahoma.

2015.summary: From Sep 2014–Aug 2015, the fund returned 2.25%, below its blended benchmark’s 10.20%, as Small Cap underperformed and Value added modest alpha while Fixed Income outpaced its index by 0.57%. AUM remained at $2.10M, and a 5% dividend ($104,000) was distributed.

2016.summary: From Sep 2015–Aug 2016, the fund delivered a 6.72% net total return, trailing its blended benchmark by 3.15%. Within sub-funds, Growth returned 1.43%, Fixed Income 2.15%, and Small Cap 12.82%. Total AUM was $0.54M, and a 5% dividend ($27,000) was paid to the University of Oklahoma.

2017.summary: From Sep 2016–Aug 2017, after paying a 5% dividend of $100,900, the fund returned 9.80% for the year (versus 11.86%), underperforming by 2.06%, and returned 2.68% in the last six months (versus 3.98%). AUM rebounded to $2.12M, and the fund’s since-inception annualized return was 5.29%, trailing by 0.74%.

2018.summary: From Sep 2017–Aug 2018, the fund returned 12.62% for the year and 5.36% in the six months ended Feb 28 2018, underperforming its benchmarks by 1.39%. The Small Cap sleeve was dissolved and the ESG sub-fund was created to launch in Jan 2019. AUM was $2.074M, and a 5% dividend ($103,700) was paid.

esg_metrics.esg_focus: Focusing on high ESG scores and avoiding companies with poor ESG ratings to mitigate downside risk and improve returns.

2019.summary: From Sep 2018–Aug 2019, the fund launched the ESG sub-fund with a $350,000 allocation, which returned 7.40% versus the S&P 500’s 6.15% over six months. The broader fund continued tactical sector bets and advisory engagements on ESG best practices. A 5% dividend was paid.

esg_metrics.esg_focus: Shifted to incorporating ESG factors into value drivers rather than relying solely on ESG screenings.

2020.summary: From Sep 2019–Aug 2020, amid COVID-driven volatility, the Growth Fund returned 37.98% over six months (Feb–Aug 2020) versus 36.93% for Russell 1000 Growth, and the ESG Fund returned 5.04% versus the S&P 500’s 3.99%. Overall allocation was 79.9% equity, 15.4% fixed income, and 4.7% cash. ESG integration deepened through the Neuberger Berman Challenge, and a 5% dividend was paid.

esg_metrics.esg_focus: Shifted to incorporating ESG factors into value drivers rather than relying solely on ESG screenings.

2021.summary: After two semesters of strong gains, MPSIF delivered a 10.28% total return for the six-month period, underperforming its 14.02% blended benchmark by 374 bps; however, combined with the prior outperformance, the fiscal-year return reached 23.13%, in line with its 23.00% blended benchmark. Assets under management peaked at $2.94 million by December 10, 2021—its highest ever—though no annual dividend was paid for the first time in MPSIF history due to COVID-related campus restrictions. The team rebalanced Growth (≈$1 million), ESG (added $140 K), and Fixed Income (added $100 K) in May to maintain sub-fund charter weights.

esg_metrics.esg_focus: Sustainable and socially responsible investing with a focus on impact.

2022.summary: In a year marked by record Fed rate hikes and tech drawdowns, the Fund realized a –8.26% total return (after its largest-ever $138.5 K dividend), outperforming its –8.72% blended benchmark by 45 bps despite negative markets. Fixed Income, Growth, and ESG sub-funds all beat their individual benchmarks, while Value lagged by 204 bps. AUM stood at $2.393 million as of December 4, 2022, with dividends cumulatively exceeding $2 million since inception.

esg_metrics.esg_focus: Focusing on sustainable practices and companies with high ESG ratings.

2023.summary: Amid geopolitical tensions and interest-rate volatility, MPSIF generated a 7.82% total return, underperforming its 10.62% blended benchmark by 281 bps over the latest six months. All equity sub-funds delivered positive absolute returns—with Growth up over 20%—but only Fixed Income outpaced its index. The Fund paid its 23rd annual 5% dividend ($123.6 K), bringing cumulative distributions to $2.1336 million, and closed the year with $2.40 million AUM.

esg_metrics.esg_focus: Investing in high ESG-performing companies to reduce risks and generate sustainable returns.

2024.summary: In the period ending August 31, 2024, MPSIF produced a 9.50% total return, narrowly lagging its 9.56% blended benchmark by 6 bps. Fixed Income led with +37 bps alpha, ESG outperformed by 326 bps, Value trailed by 21 bps, and Growth by 405 bps. Assets under management reached $2.843 million at year-end (and $3.10 million by the December 9 presentation), following the largest 5% distribution ever of $141.6 K; cumulative dividends now total $2.2752 million.
